correctness.rationale: At universality index 2 the shortest length is 2σ: two complete greedy arches require σ letters each. At that length the arches are permutations, and conversely any two permutation arches cover every ordered pair and miss xxx. For first arch increasing, length-three subsequences break into disjoint two- and three-symbol supports. An ascending pair contributes 4 and a descending pair 3. In lexicographic order the six local triple counts with all symbols distinct are 5,5,5,4,4,4. Thus the excess over 3 binom(σ,2)+4 binom(σ,3) is the sum of two nonnegative counts; the pair-count excess is already strictly positive unless Q reverses P, where both vanish. There is one word per first permutation. Uniqueness for simultaneous extremality follows at length three and existence follows from Adamson et al.'s all-length result. Independent incremental distinct-subsequence replay (python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 3) verified both local tables and all normalized second permutations at σ=2,…,8; the local support argument proves the universal claim.
